notes: §1985:IV.6.4.2.1.1 GR8 makes "A CALL statement that specifies the ON OVERFLOW, ON EXCEPTION, or NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase" a conditional statement, so without END-CALL it may not stand where a general format prints imperative-statement. callStatement takes the shared conditionalPhrases rule, whose owner table (ConditionalPhraseAssociation.Owners) gives CALL the [NOT] ON EXCEPTION pair and the positive ON OVERFLOW alone, the three phrases the 1985 rule names; VersionConformancePass.VisitCallStatement (construct call-on-overflow-removed-2023) admits ON OVERFLOW at --std 85 and refuses it at 2023. ConditionalStatements.IsConditional classifies from the parse: a CALL whose own syntax holds a statementBlock and no END-CALL is conditional, and ProcedureFormatPass.VisitStatementBlock refuses one (COBOL2796) wherever a format takes an imperative-statement; CallEmitter.EmitCall runs the phrase the activation's outcome selects. The witness is a CALL ... ON EXCEPTION inside ADD ON SIZE ERROR, refused at 85. Probes at --std 85: a CALL with ON OVERFLOW alone, and one with NOT ON EXCEPTION alone, are each refused inside ADD ON SIZE ERROR, as are a CALL ... ON OVERFLOW inside an inline PERFORM and a CALL ... ON EXCEPTION as an EVALUATE WHEN operand; the three phrases each closed by END-CALL, a CALL with no phrase, and a phrase-bearing CALL as IF's statement-1 or ending a sentence compile; at run time a CALL of a missing program takes ON OVERFLOW and ON EXCEPTION and a successful one NOT ON EXCEPTION.

next.reason: CHANGED: 1985 lists CALL with "ON OVERFLOW, ON EXCEPTION, or NOT ON EXCEPTION" (§1985:IV.6.4.2.1.1). 2023 removed the CALL ON OVERFLOW phrase (§2023:E.2 1) "On Overflow phrase of the CALL statement"): the CALL general formats (FMT-14.9.4.2, §2023:14.9.4.2) carry only "ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-1" / "NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-2", and Table 12 gives "CALL | [NOT] ON EXCEPTION | END-CALL" (§2023:14.5.1). A conforming 1985 CALL ... ON OVERFLOW is not conforming 2023 source (compile-time refusal); CALL with [NOT] ON EXCEPTION stays conditional. The Table 12 classification itself has no catalog rule (catalog lacks 14.5.1).
